questions.q: Which sequence describes the standard way to use a supervised scikit-learn model?
options: score, then fit, then predict
Create with settings, fit on training data, predict on new data, score on held-out data
predict on the training data, then fit on the test data
fit on the test set so the model sees every row
questions.explain: Construct the model with its settings, fit it on training data, then predict and score on data it has not seen.

questions.q: For a fitted LogisticRegression with classes_ equal to [0 1], what does the second column of predict_proba hold?
options: The probability of class 0
The model's confidence in its own accuracy
The probability of class 1 (churn)
The predicted class label
questions.explain: predict_proba returns one column per class in the order of model.classes_, so with [0 1] the second column is class 1.

questions.q: What does the trailing underscore in an attribute like model.coef_ tell you?
options: The attribute is private and cannot be read
It was learned during fit, so the model must be fitted first
It is a setting you passed to the constructor
It was deprecated in the latest version
questions.explain: By convention, values learned from data during fit end with an underscore. Constructor settings do not.

questions.q: In the lesson, a DummyClassifier that always predicts 'stayed' scored 0.764 and the logistic regression scored 0.768. What is the main lesson?
options: Dummy models are better than real ones
Random forests always lose to logistic regression
scikit-learn's score method is unreliable
A score needs a baseline to mean anything, and this model barely beats one
questions.explain: About 76% of customers stay, so always predicting 'stayed' is already right 76% of the time. A model must clearly beat that to be useful.

questions.q: What shapes should X and y have when passed to fit?
options: X is 2-D (rows by feature columns) and y is 1-D
Both must be 1-D
X is 1-D and y is 2-D
Both must be 3-D arrays
questions.explain: X is a table with one row per sample and one column per feature; y holds one label per row.
